Assay card records source, malignant identity and actual material rather than assuming any surviving cell represents the tumour.
Assay card records retained/added cell populations, compatibility and persistence; missing necessary biology cannot support the corresponding intervention claim.
Preparation, passage/history and selection accompany the result; a model label does not fix a stable composition.
Named substance, concentration, duration and schedule are recorded separately from an administered amount. Exposure compartment and metabolic delivery remain relevant.
The measured object, units, observation time and starting/control reference determine what an endpoint can mean.
Vehicle, positive and mechanism comparisons address alternatives; technical wells and independent biological units remain separate.
Version, threshold, quality criteria and analysis choices must be fixed before evaluation; changing them creates a different tested rule.
The card is a reading framework rather than a universal laboratory protocol, concentration cutoff or clinical readiness certificate.
Normal-cell overgrowth, malignant identity and contamination/selection require distinct checks; viable growth alone does not establish tumour attribution.
Viability, compatible donor context and functioning recognition are required for the stated immune question; mismatched donor activity can answer another question.
Human/animal compartments and measured/predicted objects remain explicit; their labels do not restore missing physiology or turn a computation into an exposure.
Dose, measured concentration and concentration over time are distinct; binding, delivery, metabolism and compartment matter. No culture concentration is adopted as a safe or achievable human dose.
Recovery, preparation delay, selection and finite viable window can shape the observed response and readiness. Named model clocks do not guarantee a result for every specimen.
Appropriate untreated/vehicle, positive and mechanism controls distinguish plausible alternatives instead of attributing every difference to the intended mechanism.
A combination requires each single intervention and a named reference model before its combined effect can be interpreted; a better combination value alone does not establish synergy.
Replicate wells measure a different unit from independent people or donors; increasing technical wells does not create more patients.
A gene perturbation/dependency result is not pharmacological inhibition, delivery, safe exposure or treatment benefit.

The fictional 100 starting, 200 control and 100 treated count yields one-half of control but no decrease from the start. It demonstrates slower net accumulation under the premises, not fifty-percent killing.

A metabolic proxy can change through physiology, cell mix or proliferation. Attributed death and recovery/regrowth need measurements that distinguish them; the unread Bookshelf chapter is not sole support.
A single-cell mass or growth-rate measurement is a distinct physical object from cell number or attributed death. A smaller positive slope can still indicate increasing mass.
Held-out donor, perturbation, cell type and laboratory test different generalisation questions; reserve all fitting and preprocessing relevant to the intended test.
The named 2025 five-task/two-task benchmark and simple baselines concern RNA perturbation prediction under defined tasks, not tumour killing or a universal statement about current AI.
A source/cell-composition mismatch can invalidate attribution even when a total signal is reproducible.
An exposure or host-compartment mismatch is not repaired by a plausible mechanism label; record dose/concentration/time rather than infer clinical achievability.
A lower endpoint than a growing control or a smaller metabolic signal is not automatically a count of cells killed.
Without single arms and the stated reference, a combined intervention does not establish the chosen synergy claim.
Preprocessing or tuning on evaluation data leaks information; a new donor test and a new perturbation test are not interchangeable.
Keep all offered specimens and quality failures visible. Missing reports are not resistant predictions and cannot be dropped from feasibility denominators.

Patient-derived culture, matrix and selection are distinct from repeatability and malignant identity. Cartry median six weeks, range four to ten, is biopsy to a colorectal drug panel; the review-reported breast median thirty-four days is establishment only. Neither forecasts a new specimen.

A viable tumour graft in a mouse has host/species, engraftment and passage constraints. Hidalgo four-to-eight months is study-ready model context; Izumchenko mean sixteen weeks begins at engraftment and ends at exposure, not the entire biopsy-to-decision process.

rows.semanticAssessment: The two-by-two cells are derived from the reported four MRI-sensitive, three dish-sensitive/MRI-intermediate and two reverse disagreements; they are not a newly observed accuracy dataset.
Dish-sensitive row is two MRI-sensitive, three MRI-intermediate, total five.
Dish-intermediate row is two MRI-sensitive, thirteen MRI-intermediate, total fifteen.
MRI column totals are four sensitive and sixteen intermediate across twenty comparisons.
No final resistant category was observed. A denominator names the conditioned group, but PPV against truth cannot be inferred from an imperfect MRI comparator.
Agreement is the two diagonal cells, (2+13)/20 = 75 percent; this is the compared subset.
Two of four MRI-sensitive cases were dish-sensitive: fifty-percent agreement conditional on the MRI-positive group, not validated clinical sensitivity against truth.
Two of five positive dish calls matched MRI: forty percent conditional agreement, not a truth-based PPV for the assay or a new patient.
Twenty-three of thirty gives approximately seventy-seven-percent usable-result coverage, with all seven assay failures retained.

Fifteen agreeing results divided by all thirty offered tumour-containing biopsies is fifty-percent matching-result yield. Seven assay failures and three untreated people remain in that denominator, unlike 15/20 agreement.

Thirteen of fifteen agreements were intermediate, positive-call MRI agreement was 2/5, and resistance performance was untested. The MRI/four-course endpoint and prespecified 55-percent target do not establish pathology, survival or care benefit.
Prospective fixation versus retrospective selection affects the validation question; either still needs a specified intended use and independent evaluation rather than a label alone.

Preserve specimen, passage/preparation, counting/model version, exposure/time, quality, prediction/no-result, threshold, independent reference/window and discordances. A later revision must not rewrite the original record.

The later hypothetical version two investigates three discordant sensitive dish calls against MRI, not three known truth errors. Freeze the original, revise the rule and evaluate a new reserved group.

A revision creates a new claim. Reuse of original observations is development information and cannot masquerade as independent validation.
Investigate identity, preparation, exposure, timing, endpoint/comparator and missing biology before interpreting disagreement; neither forced harmonisation nor automatic rejection is justified.

Blood sampling and regional imaging measure different objects and can complement each other. A finite sample does not inventory every site/population, and an observed course does not isolate one drug as its cause.
Changing disease, treatment or setting changes the use claim; advanced-treatment evidence cannot automatically validate an unrelated postoperative question.
MRI shrinkage, pathology, blood and survival are not the same outcome; a named bridge is needed for substitution.
Hidden no-result cases distort reportability and inference. They remain unknown rather than being relabelled negatives or dropped.
Editing a rule or its recorded prediction after the outcome is known changes the claim and must retain the original version.
A revised version evaluated on the same cases uses development information; an independent new reserved set addresses the next claim.
One observed course, especially with multiple interventions, cannot establish what would have happened under another strategy.

Vlachogiannis selected advanced gastrointestinal comparisons reported 100-percent sensitivity, 93-percent specificity, 88-percent PPV and 100-percent NPV in twenty-one comparisons. They are not twenty-one automatically independent people or universal eighty-eight-percent accuracy.

Ooft abstract supports irinotecan-lesion response prediction and failure for fluorouracil/oxaliplatin. The sixty-one enrollment count is attributed to NKI first-party news; the review supplies twenty-nine compared patients and ten/twelve irinotecan regimen groups, not a claimed fresh read of the unavailable original body.

Boileve eighty-seven pretreated advanced pancreatic patients, fifty-four organoids, thirty-four evaluable and mean 6.8 weeks retain 83.3/92.9-percent study performance. Routine hit/non-hit associations are not randomised model-guided benefit.

Izumchenko 1163 tumours, 578 engraftments (reported 49 percent), ninety-two people and 129 treatment comparisons are distinct. The 112/129 (87 percent) positive grouping includes stable disease with CR/PR; sensitivity 96 and specificity 70 coexist with only 91/129 exact category agreement.

Wensink review has seventeen publications, five colorectal and seven metastatic, with pooled establishment about sixty-eight percent, sensitivity eighty-one and specificity seventy-four. Author warnings about selection, quantitative-reporting and unfixed index tests qualify the pooled estimates.
Five-patterns introduction only; every substantive pattern is assessed separately.
Thirty-four evaluable out of eighty-seven enrolled is approximately thirty-nine percent, a different denominator from establishment or within-evaluable performance.
A result for irinotecan need not transfer to fluorouracil/oxaliplatin; an assay/drug combination needs evidence for the actual intervention.

Replace the unsupported blanket most-studies statement with named advanced selected cohorts and the review counts of five colorectal/seven metastatic among seventeen. Their populations do not automatically establish postoperative early-breast use.
Scan response and progression are not survival or improved care; endpoint substitution requires its own intended-context evidence.

Retain the review authors warning of possible overestimation, selective quantitative reporting, unfixed index tests and possible publication bias. Do not assert a measured prevalence of unpublished negative studies.
Agreement with an outcome and benefit from a strategy that acts on the result are distinct; the relevant comparison must evaluate the intended decision.

SENSOR sixty-one enrolled, fifty-four eligible, thirty-one organoids, twenty-five eight-drug screens, nineteen hits and six treated (three each vistusertib/capivasertib) yielded zero objective responses. This bounded strategy result does not show all organoid testing ineffective.

EXALT 143 tested, fifty-six assay-guided and thirty meeting the PFS-ratio endpoint retain the previous-treatment comparator. Body/protocol threshold is at least 1.3, not a newly invented randomized control.

EXALT previous-therapy and twenty physician-choice observations are nonrandomized. LN, marrow and blood inputs are named without a universal easier-sampling claim. A 2021 organoid review cannot establish a current no-solid-tumour-RCT statement contradicted by Ranjan 2023.
Guillen breast platform includes one TNBC complete response. That supports feasibility/a signal rather than comparative model-guided benefit or a patient-specific forecast.

Performance statistics do not themselves establish care improvement; named strategy comparisons retain population, design and endpoint limits.
A selected single response does not estimate general effectiveness or establish the counterfactual treatment course.
